title: agentdag result record
description: The ONLY thing the coordinator branches on (design 2.2). Every node, whatever ran it, returns one of these on completion, written to nodes/<node_id>/<hash8>/record.json.

node_id.description: The node this record belongs to.

attempt.description: Which attempt produced this record; matches the node spec's attempt (2.1).

status.description: The coordinator branches only on this typed field (2.2). done: the work succeeded. failed: it was attempted and did not succeed. blocked / needs_context: it could not proceed and the record says why. cancelled: the scheduler stopped it (deadline or cancel). needs_continuation: the node hit its context ceiling and wrote a handover record for a successor (design 3.8). refused: a decision or a policy declined it - an approve rejection marks the branch that produced the payload refused. There is no 'rejected' value (design 2.2, C5).

artefact_refs.description: References (paths under the node's artefact dir) to the content this node produced. Content lives under the node's artefact dir, never in the record (2.2).

key_facts.description: A small typed map the brief's output schema defines; free-form here since the shape varies per node/brief (2.2).

typed_fields.description: The key_facts keys the brief declared as TYPED. The coordinator may branch only on a key named here (design 3.3, M7); every other key_facts entry is free text it must not inspect.

charged_tokens.description: What the cap actually charged for this dispatch, per model row - equals measured tokens when the executor reports them, else the node's full token budget (design 3.4/5, decided 2026-08-17).

cost_usd.description: What the dispatch cost in USD, as the executor itself reported it (the Claude CLI's own total_cost_usd on its terminal message); null when it reported none, which is not the same statement as 0 (a subscription row costs nothing at the margin). Recorded so a coordinator run and a single-agent control run, whose harness reports the same figure, are comparable in one unit.

tokens.description: Measured token usage for this dispatch per field; a field is null when the executor does not report it (Codex reports none in the MCP result; reconciled later from its rollout log).

cache_write.description: Cache-creation tokens: what the dispatch spent WRITING the prompt cache, a component of 'in' (the input total) that the total alone cannot recover. Optional, never a required-but-nullable property: a tokens block written before this field existed omits the key entirely, and must keep omitting it on re-dump, because record_hash feeds every downstream node's journal key and an added 'cache_write': null would re-key work already on disk.

duration_s.description: Wall-clock duration of the dispatch, in seconds.

executor_used.description: The actual executor that ran this node (e.g. 'claude', 'mcp:codex/codex'); may differ from the spec's executor after a clamp (2.3 rule 4).

model_used.description: The actual model alias used, after any tier-policy resolution or clamp.

effort_used.description: The actual effort level used, after any tier-policy resolution or clamp.

knowledge_used.description: Recorded from day one so the journal can later validate on used-datasets instead of allowed-datasets (2.2, 3.2).

dataset.description: The knowledge-index dataset name actually read from.

content_hash.description: Content-addressed hash of the dataset state at read time.

input_hash.description: The journal key this record was dispatched under: v2:sha256(prefix_hash + NUL + canonical(spec)) per design 3.2. Rendered here as 'v2:sha256:<64 hex chars>'; the exact separator/encoding is an implementation choice the design leaves open.

sandbox.description: What sandbox boundary was actually in force for this node (Task 19), stamped by the coordinator from the wired Sandbox adapter's own declaration. Absent on any record from before this field existed (the M2 runs' own journals carry none) - optional, never a required-but-nullable property, so those still validate.

adapter.description: Which adapter produced this: "none" | "container" | "vm" - free text, not a closed enum, so a later adapter needs no schema change to name itself.

filesystem.description: Whether the node is blocked from reaching paths outside its declared mounts.

network_egress.description: Whether the node's outbound network access is restricted to an allowlist.

separate_uid.description: Whether the node runs as an operating-system user distinct from the coordinator's own.

error.description: Present when status is failed, blocked, needs_context, refused or cancelled.

type.description: The closed error vocabulary of design 2.2. agents_empty_result: no artefact refs AND no required key_facts key (design 9). auth_failure: the executor's credential was rejected - non-transient, fails the run, never escalates a tier (3.4). deadline: the node's dispatch was interrupted at a turn seam once elapsed wall-clock time exceeded deadline_s (2.2, M3) - the node's OS-level scope is untouched by this; only a whole-run cancel (3.4) kills a scope. knowledge_unavailable: a declared knowledge dataset could not be read, so the node returns needs_context rather than done (3.7). rate_limited: the model provider refused the dispatch for quota, not for a bad credential - the CLI reports both as authentication_failed, so this member exists only because an out-of-band probe told them apart; it suspends the run resumably rather than failing it. continuation_limit: the node exhausted max_continuations.

transient.description: Whether this failure is transient (executor error, timeout below the deadline). Only a transient failure record permits a same-tier retry for a map branch (2.3 rule 5).

continuation.description: Which link of a handover chain produced this record (3.8); 0 for a node that never handed over. Counts handovers that carry work FORWARD, where attempt counts tries at the same work. Absent on a line written before 3.8, so it is not required.

error.message: no artefact refs and no required key_facts key
